judgment.rationale: The supplied log gives maintainers a concrete provider-load failure to investigate. It does not establish that the driver update caused the blank window or that a specific provider is responsible.
evidence: The report describes a blank window after installing 0.103.3151.
The attached log shows InvalidCastException with HRESULT 0x80004002 in the TopLevelCommands ABI call from LoadTopLevelCommands.
judgment.recommended_action: Compare provider load and visible command population on a clean profile and an in-place update using the reported build.

issue_context.summary: CmdPal opens with no visible commands after installation. The log shows a provider interop failure during top-level command enumeration.
known_information: The reported build is 0.103.3151 installed from GitHub.
The screenshot and CmdPal log were supplied; a full Bug Report ZIP was not attached.
inferences: A provider activation or interface compatibility failure may contribute to the empty command list. The observed exception does not prove that it affects all providers.
issue_context.analysis: Separate host-wide command population from a failure in one provider. Check which provider fails, whether other providers still load, and whether the same behavior occurs on a clean profile before changing interop handling.
initial_investigation: Checked the issue timeline and searched for matching reports and linked PRs; no covering work was found.
Read the provider-load stack in the supplied log and traced the top-level command request in CommandProviderWrapper. No runtime reproduction or driver attribution was made.

fix_assessment.rationale: The failure points to command-provider enumeration, but the contributing provider and the relationship between the exception and empty UI must be established before choosing a compatibility or recovery change.

proposed_fixes.title: Correct the demonstrated CmdPal provider-load failure
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: a provider does not expose the expected interface at load time, and the resulting failure may leave command population incomplete.
plan: Identify the failing provider and its interface version using the failed command enumeration in a test profile.
Trace whether successful providers still populate the UI. Correct the demonstrated compatibility or recovery boundary without suppressing the provider failure diagnostic.
verification: Compare clean-install and in-place update behavior.
Verify that healthy providers remain visible if one provider cannot load.

confidence.rationale: The log identifies an interop boundary but does not establish the provider or prove that this exception causes the entire window to be empty.

actions.label: Trace CmdPal provider loading after installation

reproduce.version_requirement: PowerToys 0.103.3151 and the current stable release
prerequisites: Use a disposable Windows profile or VM; keep the reporter's existing profile and settings untouched.
steps: Install 0.103.3151 on a clean test profile, launch CmdPal, and record whether built-in commands appear.
Repeat with an in-place update on a separate test profile and record per-provider load outcomes and the visible command count.
If command enumeration produces HRESULT 0x80004002, identify the provider and check whether other providers still populate the window after relaunch.
reproduce.expected_result: CmdPal displays commands from healthy providers after install or update; an unavailable provider does not leave the entire window blank.
